BACKEND SHARED DECISIONS (every backend brief follows these; the reference design, BACKEND_SPEC.md and API_CONTRACT.md win if anything here disagrees)

0. Brief map (who owns what; read the owner's code before using it)
Wave 1: be-01 scaffold and app skeleton (installs every package), be-02 store and rate limits, be-03 knowledge base and system prompt, be-04 mail service and all email templates, be-05 booking rules and calendar/meeting contracts, be-06 Google Calendar (Meet) and Zoom providers. Wave 2: be-07 chat service, be-08 chat route, be-09 contact route, be-10 availability and booking info routes, be-11 booking route (.ics and both emails). Wave 3: be-12 API contract and security tests, be-13 live check scripts and google:auth, be-14 README and deploy notes. A brief starts when its deps passed review, even inside the same wave.

1. Stack and exact versions (installed ONCE by be-01; nobody else runs npm install)
dependencies: express 5.2.1, helmet 8.3.0, cors 2.8.6, express-rate-limit 8.7.0, pino 10.3.1, pino-http 11.0.0, zod 4.6.5, dotenv 18.0.4, openai 7.23.0, nodemailer 10.0.12 (ships its own types), googleapis 182.0.0, ics 3.12.0, date-fns 4.4.0, date-fns-tz 3.2.0.
devDependencies: typescript 6.0.3 (NOT 7.x: typescript-eslint 8.71 needs typescript <6.1), tsx 4.23.15, @types/node 24.19.0, @types/express 5.0.6, @types/cors 2.8.19, vitest 5.0.2, vite 8.3.1 (peer of vitest 5), @vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.2, supertest 7.3.0, @types/supertest 7.2.1, eslint 10.11.0, @eslint/js 10.0.1, typescript-eslint 8.71.0, eslint-config-prettier 10.1.8, globals 17.12.0, prettier 3.9.9, pino-pretty 13.1.3.
Node >= 24 (Node 24 LTS on the VPS; the dev machine runs Node 26). ESM ("type": "module"), module and moduleResolution NodeNext, relative imports end in ".js". TypeScript strict, no `any` without a comment. Zoom is called with the built-in fetch (no Zoom SDK).
npm scripts (be-01 writes package.json; the named script files come from later briefs): dev (tsx watch --clear-screen=false --include "src/**/*" src/server.ts), dev:fake (the same with DEV_FAKE_EXTERNALS=true), build (tsc -p tsconfig.build.json), start (node dist/server.js), typecheck (tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit), lint (eslint .), format, format:check, test (vitest run), test:watch, test:coverage, google:auth (tsx scripts/google-auth.ts), check:env, check:chat, check:contact, check:booking (tsx scripts/check-env.ts and so on), mail:preview (tsx scripts/mail-preview.ts).

2. Folder layout (backend/)
src/app.ts, src/server.ts, src/config/env.ts, src/lib/ (logger, errors, lifecycle: be-01; dailyCap, idempotency, keyedMutex: be-02), src/middleware/ (be-01, plus rateLimit.ts from be-02), src/validators/ (common.ts be-01; chat.ts be-08; contact.ts be-09; bookingInfo.ts be-10; booking.ts be-11), src/routes/ (types.ts, index.ts, health.routes.ts: be-01; one <feature>.routes.ts per feature), src/controllers/, src/store/ (be-02), src/knowledge/portfolio.json and src/services/knowledge/ (be-03), src/services/chat/ (prompt.ts be-03; the rest be-07), src/services/mail/ and src/templates/ (be-04), src/services/contact/ (be-09), src/services/booking/ (catalog.ts, time.ts, types.ts be-05; availability.ts be-10; ics.ts, bookingService.ts, emailData.ts be-11), src/services/calendar/ and src/services/meeting/ (types.ts and calendar/fake.ts be-05; real providers and index.ts factories be-06), scripts/ (tsx scripts: mail-preview.ts be-04, the rest be-13), tests/ (Vitest, one folder per area; tests/helpers/testEnv, testApp and logCapture be-01; fixtures and fullApp be-12), deploy/ (examples only, be-14).

3. Layers
routes (path plus per-route middleware) -> controllers (parseInput with zod, call one service, shape the JSON) -> services (business logic, no Express types, clock injected as now: () => Date) -> adapters (OpenRouter, SMTP, Google Calendar, Zoom) behind small interfaces, each with a fake for dev and tests.

4. Feature module contract (be-01 owns src/routes/types.ts and src/routes/index.ts)
- interface AppContext { env: Env; logger: Logger; lifecycle: Lifecycle }
- interface ApiModule { name: string; createRouter(ctx: AppContext): Router | Promise<Router> }
- Each feature route file default-exports an ApiModule built by an exported factory create<Feature>Module(overrides?) so tests can inject fakes (store, services, clock).
- src/routes/index.ts loads the allowlist ['chat', 'contact', 'booking-info', 'booking'] from `./${name}.routes.js` with dynamic import, so no feature edits a shared file. Outside production a missing or broken module is skipped with a warning (the dev server keeps running while features are built); in production it is fatal.
- Every module router is mounted at /api. Inside a module router attach middleware per route (router.post('/chat', limiter, handler)). Never call router.use() without a path: each module router also sees the requests of modules mounted after it, so a path-less limiter would count other endpoints.
- Paths: chat.routes.ts POST /chat; contact.routes.ts POST /contact; booking-info.routes.ts GET /booking/slots and GET /booking/config; booking.routes.ts POST /booking. GET and HEAD /api/health are built in by be-01.

5. App pipeline (be-01, src/app.ts, in this order)
trust proxy (TRUST_PROXY, default 1), x-powered-by off, request id (accept X-Request-Id if it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$/, else crypto.randomUUID(); echo it), pino-http, helmet, cors allowlist (CORS_ORIGINS; methods GET, POST, OPTIONS; allowed headers Content-Type, Idempotency-Key, X-Request-Id; exposed headers Retry-After, X-Request-Id; credentials off; maxAge 600), Cache-Control: no-store on /api, JSON body parser (32 KB everywhere except POST /api/chat, which gets 64 KB), health, module routers, not found, error handler. No compression middleware (it breaks SSE; nginx can gzip).

6. Error envelope and statuses (be-01, src/lib/errors.ts)
{ ok: false, error: { code, message, fields? } }. VALIDATION_ERROR 400 (413 when the body is over the limit, 400 for malformed JSON), RATE_LIMITED 429 plus Retry-After in seconds, SLOT_TAKEN 409, UPSTREAM_ERROR 502 (503 when the feature is not configured), NOT_FOUND 404, INTERNAL 500. Throw AppError or use the Errors helpers; Express 5 forwards rejected promises, so no asyncHandler wrapper. Never send stack traces, upstream error text or secrets to the client. Success bodies start with ok: true.
Default messages (plain English, no em dashes): VALIDATION_ERROR "Some fields need a quick fix.", RATE_LIMITED "Too many requests. Please try again later.", SLOT_TAKEN "That time was just taken. Please pick another slot.", UPSTREAM_ERROR "The service is busy right now. Please try again.", NOT_FOUND "Not found.", INTERNAL "Something went wrong. Please try again."

7. Validation (zod 4 on every input and on env)
Controllers call parseInput(schema, data) from src/middleware/validate.ts; it throws VALIDATION_ERROR with fields keyed by the top-level field name (nested paths joined with dots, for example history.3.content), first message per key. Shared pieces in src/validators/common.ts (be-01): EMAIL_RE copied from the reference (L5185) /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@.]+(\.[^\s@.]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/, PHONE_RE /^[+()\d\s.\-]{7,24}$/ (reference L5668), emailSchema(max), trimmedString(min, max), optionalTrimmed(max) (missing becomes ""), honeypotSchema, isHoneypotFilled(v), ianaTimeZoneSchema, ymdDateSchema (YYYY-MM-DD and a real calendar date). Unknown keys are stripped, never an error. Contact caps are the reference maxlengths (API_CONTRACT.md). Server caps for booking fields the reference leaves open: name 2..200, email max 254, phone max 60 (no pattern, as in the reference), company max 200, notes max 800.

8. Env (be-01, src/config/env.ts)
parseEnv(source) is pure; loadEnv() runs dotenv quietly (never overriding real env vars) and then parseEnv. Empty strings count as unset. On failure print variable names and reasons, never values, and exit 1. Variables and defaults: NODE_ENV (development | test | production, default development), HOST (127.0.0.1), PORT (8787), LOG_LEVEL (info; silent when NODE_ENV=test), TRUST_PROXY (1), CORS_ORIGINS (comma list of origins; default http://localhost:3000,http://127.0.0.1:3000 outside production; required in production), SITE_URL (https://faisalhanif.work), DEV_FAKE_EXTERNALS (false; refused in production), OPENROUTER_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_MODEL (no model name in code), OPENROUTER_FALLBACK_MODELS (comma list, default empty), CHAT_MAX_TOKENS (600, 50..4000), CHAT_DAILY_GLOBAL_LIMIT (1000), SMTP_HOST (smtp.gmail.com), SMTP_PORT (465), SMTP_SECURE (true), SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, MAIL_FROM (default "Faisal Hanif <SMTP_USER>"), MAIL_TO_OWNER, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN, GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID (primary), BOOKING_TIMEZONE (Asia/Karachi), ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_ID, ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET.
Keys stay optional so the server boots before the owner adds them. features(env) -> { chat, mail, google, zoom } (chat needs key and model; mail needs SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS and MAIL_TO_OWNER; google needs the three GOOGLE_ secrets; zoom needs the three ZOOM_ values; with DEV_FAKE_EXTERNALS chat, mail and google count as available, zoom always follows its real config). The server logs one warning listing unconfigured features. An endpoint whose feature is not configured returns 503 UPSTREAM_ERROR, so the frontend uses the reference fallback (local responder or error toast). Booking needs google and mail.

9. Dev fakes (DEV_FAKE_EXTERNALS=true, npm run dev:fake; refused in production)
In-process fakes replace OpenRouter (be-07: a short reply in the reference chat format picked from the knowledge base), SMTP (be-04: writes each message to backend/tmp/mail/<timestamp>-<tag>.html and .txt plus attachments, logs only the tag and file path, never the subject because it holds a name) and Google Calendar (be-05: events in memory, freebusy from them, a clearly fake Meet link such as https://meet.google.com/dev-fake-abc). Zoom always follows the real config, so picking Zoom in dev tests the meetLink: null path. Tests use the same fakes (or in-memory variants) through the module factory overrides.

10. Store and limits (be-02)
Store = CounterStore + KeyValueStore + close(); MemoryStore implements it; getSharedStore(ctx) is the process singleton (registers close on shutdown). Rate limit counters, the chat daily cap, idempotency records, contact dedupe, the freebusy cache and the recently booked set all go through it, so Redis can replace it later without code changes. Limits (RATE_LIMITS in src/middleware/rateLimit.ts): chat 8 per minute and 60 per day per IP; contact 5 per hour; booking 3 per hour; booking-info (slots and config) 60 per minute; chat global cap CHAT_DAILY_GLOBAL_LIMIT per BOOKING_TIMEZONE calendar day (200 with a friendly reply, not 429). 429 bodies use the envelope with RATE_LIMITED and a Retry-After header.

11. Logging
Root pino logger from src/lib/logger.ts; inside requests use req.log. Log event names, request ids, statuses, timings, model names, counts and booking ids. Never log secrets, chat text, names, emails, phone numbers, companies, notes or IP addresses. logger.ts also sets redaction paths as a second line of defence. pino-pretty only when NODE_ENV=development and stdout is a TTY.

12. Lifecycle
ctx.lifecycle.onStarted(name, fn) runs after the server listens (SMTP verify, config warnings; failures only log). ctx.lifecycle.onShutdown(name, fn) runs on SIGTERM or SIGINT after the server stops taking connections (store close, SMTP close). Shutdown timeout 10 s, then exit 1.

13. Booking rules (be-05 src/services/booking/catalog.ts and time.ts are the single source)
quick = "Quick Chat", 30 min, $15; deep = "Technical Deep Dive", 60 min, $25; sessions 1..10; currency USD; hourly starts 09:00..17:00 in BOOKING_TIMEZONE on the calendar day `date` (reference slotsFor L6060: Date.UTC(y, m-1, d, h-5) for h 9..17); `date` must be Mon..Fri; start at least 2 hours from now; platforms "Google Meet" | "Zoom". Date window: the reference calendar allows days after the visitor's today and at most 60 days ahead by the visitor's own clock, so POST /booking checks `date` against today in the payload `timezone` (tomorrow .. today + 60 days). GET /booking/slots has no time zone, so it serves any weekday from today to today + 61 days in BOOKING_TIMEZONE (the widest range any visitor can pick) and returns an empty list outside it. Shape errors (not a real date, a weekend, a startUtc that is not one of that date's slots, a bad session or platform) are 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; timing and availability errors (date outside the window, under 2 hours notice, busy on the calendar or recently booked) are 409 SLOT_TAKEN, so the frontend reloads the slots. A slot is busy when [start, start + duration) overlaps a freebusy interval or a recently booked slot.

14. Chat output format (what the reference renderer L6333-6341 and fromText L6377-6386 can show)
Paragraphs separated by one blank line; lines inside a paragraph are joined with spaces; a block is a list only when EVERY line starts with "- ", "* ", "• " or "1. "; all list blocks are merged into one list and any paragraph after the first list moves below it, so a reply has at most one list, with a blank line before and after it; **bold** without nested asterisks; links only as [label](url) with https://, http://, mailto:, tel: or #. No headings, tables, code blocks, inline code, images or HTML. The server sanitizer (be-07) enforces this.

15. Tests
Vitest + Supertest under backend/tests/ (node environment). tests/setup.ts replaces global fetch with a function that throws "Real network calls are blocked in tests" unless a test mocks it. OpenRouter, Google, Zoom and SMTP are always mocked or faked; no test needs a .env file, the network or a running server. Build apps with buildTestApp() (tests/helpers/testApp.ts) and env with makeTestEnv(overrides) (tests/helpers/testEnv.ts); every test gets a fresh MemoryStore through the module factory overrides. Each brief tests its own files; be-12 adds the cross-endpoint contract and security suite.

16. Worker rules (each brief repeats the key ones)
Quote the project path (it has a space before the slash). You may be a restart: FIRST list and read the files you own that already exist, keep finished work, continue from there, never start over. Work in small steps, write files in pieces, and make a tool call at least every few minutes. Touch only owned files; report anything else you need. Only be-01 runs npm install; if a package is missing, stop and report. Never run git. Only be-01 runs npm run build. From wave 2 on the orchestrator keeps the backend running on http://localhost:8787 (npm run dev:fake); never start a server on 8787 yourself, use it for curl smoke checks (tsx watch reloads your files). Run from backend/: npm run typecheck, npx eslint <your files>, npx prettier --check <your files>, npx vitest run <your tests>. Ignore errors that come only from files other workers are still writing, but list them. Check library APIs with Context7 (resolve-library-id, then query-docs) before coding against them. Plain English in all new text (logs, errors, emails, docs), no em dashes. End with a report: files written, checks and results, exported names later briefs use, open items.

briefs.brief:
You are be-02 (wave 1, after be-01). Build the storage abstraction and every abuse control primitive the features use. Nothing here knows about chat, contact or booking payloads.

RULES: project root "/Users/faisalhanif/MyProfile/My Projects /Faisal-Website" (quote it); work in backend/. Read .claude/prd/BACKEND_SPEC.md, API_CONTRACT.md and the sharedDecisions of .claude/plans/backend-plan.json (from the root: node -e "console.log(require('./.claude/plans/backend-plan.json').sharedDecisions)"). You may be a restart: FIRST read the owned files that exist and continue from there; never start over. Work in small steps and write files in pieces. Touch only OWNS. Never run npm install, git, npm run build or a server on 8787. Read be-01's src/config/env.ts, src/lib/errors.ts, src/routes/types.ts and tests/helpers/* before coding. Check the express-rate-limit 8 Store interface (init, increment, decrement, resetKey, prefix, localKeys), handler, standardHeaders and ipKeyGenerator with Context7.

1. src/store/types.ts
- CounterStore { increment(key, windowMs): Promise<{ count: number; resetAt: number }>; decrement(key): Promise<void>; reset(key): Promise<void> } (fixed window that starts on the first hit).
- KeyValueStore { get<T>(key): Promise<T | undefined>; set<T>(key, value, ttlMs): Promise<void>; setIfAbsent<T>(key, value, ttlMs): Promise<boolean>; delete(key): Promise<void> }.
- Store extends both with close(): Promise<void>. Values must be JSON serialisable (document it) so a Redis store can replace this without changing callers.

2. src/store/memoryStore.ts: MemoryStore implements Store; options { now?: () => number; maxEntries?: 50000; sweepIntervalMs?: 60000 }. Lazy expiry on read plus an unref'd sweep timer; over maxEntries evict the entries closest to expiry; store structuredClone copies; close() clears the timer and maps.

3. src/store/index.ts: createStore(env) (MemoryStore today; a comment shows where Redis plugs in), getSharedStore(ctx) (process singleton; registers ctx.lifecycle.onShutdown('store', ...) once), resetSharedStoreForTests().

4. src/middleware/rateLimit.ts
- RATE_LIMITS = { chatPerMinute 8 per 60 s, chatPerDay 60 per 24 h, contact 5 per hour, booking 3 per hour, bookingInfo 60 per minute } as const.
- createRateLimiter({ name, windowMs, limit, store: CounterStore, keyGenerator? }): express-rate-limit 8 with a CounterStoreAdapter (prefix `rl:${name}:`), the current standard headers option, legacyHeaders false, default key ipKeyGenerator(req.ip) so IPv6 users are grouped by subnet. Handler: Retry-After in whole seconds (at least 1) and the 429 envelope from Errors.rateLimited; log warn "rate_limited" with the limiter name only (never the IP).
- rateLimiters(store) -> { chatPerMinute, chatPerDay, contact, booking, bookingInfo }. A comment explains that features attach them per route, never with a path-less router.use (sharedDecisions 4).

5. src/lib/dailyCap.ts: createDailyCap({ store, name, limit, timeZone, now? }) -> { consume(): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; count: number; limit: number }> }. Key `cap:${name}:${YYYY-MM-DD in timeZone}`, window until the next local midnight (date-fns-tz), allowed false once count > limit. Used for the chat global cap.

6. src/lib/idempotency.ts: createIdempotency<T>({ store, prefix, ttlMs, now? }) -> { run(key, fingerprint, work): Promise<{ replayed: boolean; value: T }>; peek(key) }. Give them one command per feature that exercises it against the real service, plus the helper that produces GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN. Scripts call the services in process (no HTTP server needed) and read backend/.env through loadEnv().

1. scripts/lib/cli.ts: parseFlags(argv), ok/warn/fail line printers (plain text, no colours required), requireFeatures(env, names) (prints the missing variable names, never values, and exits 1), a runMain(fn) wrapper (exit codes, no stack traces for expected failures), and a createScriptContext(env) that builds the AppContext the service factories need (logger at warn so the output stays readable).

2. check-env.ts (no network): each feature's status from features(env) with missing variable names; format warnings (Gmail App Password containing spaces, MAIL_TO_OWNER not an email, CORS_ORIGINS without https://faisalhanif.work when NODE_ENV=production, DEV_FAKE_EXTERNALS set). Exit 0 when everything configured is valid, 1 otherwise.

3. check-chat.ts: getChatService with the real OpenRouter model; asks four questions (rates, one project, one technical question, one prompt injection that asks for the system prompt); prints each reply, model, attempts and latency; fails when the rates reply lacks "$25", a reply breaks the sharedDecisions 14 format, or the injection reply contains a line of the system prompt. --model <id> overrides OPENROUTER_MODEL for one run.

4. check-contact.ts: verifies SMTP first. Without --send it only renders both emails and reports the SMTP result. With --send it submits sample data through the contact service with the visitor email set to --to <address> (default MAIL_TO_OWNER), so exactly two real emails arrive: the owner email and the confirmation.

5. check-booking.ts: default dry run: Google auth works (a freeBusy call for the next 7 days), prints free slots for the next three weekdays, and checks the Zoom token when Zoom is configured. --create books the next free slot through the booking service (visitor --to, default MAIL_TO_OWNER; --platform "Google Meet" or Zoom; --session quick or deep), then prints booking id, meet link and event link. --cleanup deletes that event afterwards; --delete <eventId> removes an old test event. Never books without --create.

6. scripts/lib/googleAuthFlow.ts and google-auth.ts (npm run google:auth): needs GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET from a Desktop app OAuth client. Starts a loopback server on 127.0.0.1 (a free port), builds the consent URL with access_type offline, prompt consent, be-06's GOOGLE_CALENDAR_SCOPES and a random state, opens the browser (open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux, else prints the URL), checks state on the callback, exchanges the code, prints the refresh token ONCE with the line to paste into backend/.env, and closes the server. It never writes the token to a file or a log. A 5 minute timeout. It warns that a consent screen left in Testing issues tokens that expire after 7 days, so the owner should publish the app.

7. Tests for the pure parts: parseFlags, requireFeatures output (names only), buildAuthUrl (offline, consent, scopes, redirect), state mismatch rejected, callback parsing.

Frontend-lead: (a) the contact body must include startedAt (ms epoch when the form was first shown) and the hidden website field. A submit under 3 s gets 400 fields.startedAt, and the frontend shows the reference error toast. (b) POST /api/booking should send an Idempotency-Key header (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,128}$/, for example a uuid), one per submit attempt and reused on a retry of that attempt. (c) In dev, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8787. CORS allows http://localhost:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:3000 by default. (d) GET /api/booking/slots returns [] for a date outside the window and 400 for a weekend. A 409 from POST sends the visitor back to step 2.

API_CONTRACT.md: approve these additions. None of them changes the UI. (1) With ?stream=true, an error after streaming began is sent as `event: error` with data {code, message}, then the stream ends. (2) A filled honeypot on POST /api/booking returns a normal-looking 200 and creates nothing. (3) A contact submit that comes too fast returns 400 with fields.startedAt. (4) The POST /api/booking date window (tomorrow up to 60 days) is checked in the payload timezone, matching the reference calendar, which uses the visitor's own clock. GET /booking/slots serves the widest possible range (today to +61 days in PKT). The lead adds these lines to the contract at review if approved.
